title: SIEM ingest validation and RBACv2 evidence scenarios
summary: Working playbook for validating SIEM ingest from RBAC v2 audit exports and preparing auditor-friendly evidence. Includes live test scenarios, synthetic event generator notes, deterministic export checks, and suggested Q&A responses for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 reviews.
purpose: Provide a repeatable validation and evidence-collection process that proves our auditlog export schema, RBAC v2 events, and SIEM pipeline meet control objectives for integrity, retention, and traceability required by SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audits.
scope: Applies to RBAC v2 auditlog exports, the SIEM ingestion pipeline (Kafka -> log-transform -> ES/chronicle), automated evidence bundles, and the auditor-facing packet we deliver for access-control and logging controls. Excludes endpoint instrumentation code not part of the current export contract.
background: As RBAC v2 rolled out we added ephemeral grants, delegation events, and richer principal metadata. The SIEM export schema was extended to carry grant_id, session_id, principal_fingerprints, and signed-batch checksums. Auditors have asked for deterministic proofs that logs are complete, unmodified, and mapped to control requirements. This doc collects test cases and an evidence checklist we can run pre-audit.
siem_export_schema_overview: Our canonical export batch is a gzipped JSONL file with a manifest header. Fields of interest: event_id, timestamp_utc, tenant_id, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource, grant_id (nullable), session_id (nullable), pre_state, post_state, request_id, ingestion_offset, batch_checksum_sha256, signer_key_id. The manifest includes start_offset, end_offset, earliest_ts, latest_ts, record_count, and signer_key_id. SIEM transforms must preserve timestamp_utc and ingestion_offset and surface batch_checksum_sha256 to the final index for sampling verification.
validation_test_scenarios: 1) Full-batch replay: generate a synthetic 10k-event batch with a mixture of create/delete/update/grant/revoke and confirm manifest checksums match the on-disk archive. 2) Ephemeral grant lifecycle: create grant -> use -> auto-expire -> revoke; confirm grant_id appears in pre_state/post_state for all relevant events. 3) Delegation chain: A delegates to B, B acts on resource -> ensure chain is preserved in principal_chain field. 4) Partial-loss simulation: drop 0.1% of events in transform stage and confirm sampling scripts detect gap via ingestion_offset discontinuity. 5) Time-drift windowing: inject events with out-of-order timestamps and ensure SIEM reordering policy and earliest_ts/latest_ts in manifest align with final index. 6) Fuzz malformed metadata: send events missing principal_fingerprint and ensure pipeline routes to quarantine topic and incident alert is generated.
evidence_collection_steps: Step 1: Run synthetic generator (tools/siem-test-gen) with test tenant 'audit-playground' to produce a signed batch. Step 2: Archive the batch to s3://redwood-audit/qa-playground/YYYYMMDD/. Step 3: Trigger normal pipeline ingest and wait for ES indexing. Step 4: Run verify_batch.sh which checks gz integrity, recomputes sha256 and compares with manifest, then queries ES for ingestion_offset range and record_count. Step 5: Produce auditor packet: bundle manifest, gz, verifier logs, ES query results (hit counts), and signer public key fingerprint. Step 6: Register the packet in Jira SEC-412 and notify auditor mailbox with checksum and retrieval instructions.
evidence_acceptance_criteria: - Checksums: recomputed batch_checksum_sha256 must match manifest exactly. - Completeness: ES hit_count for ingestion_offset range must equal manifest.record_count. - Traceability: every action event must include either grant_id or session_id when applicable. - Retention proof: archived object must have S3 version id and object-lock retention metadata preserved. - Signed delivery: packet includes signer_key_id and public key mapping and a notarized TTR (time-to-receipt) stamp.
rbac_v2_control_mapping_summary: Map RBAC v2 artifacts to typical control objectives: CC6.1/CC6.2 (access monitoring) => event presence for access/grant/revoke; CC7.x (change management) => pre_state/post_state snapshots; CC5.x (logical access) => principal_type and principal_fingerprint; ISO A.9 (access control) => retention and proof-of-delivery of exports; ISO A.12.4 (logging & monitoring) => export manifest, signed checksum, and SIEM alerting for anomalies.
identified_gaps_and_risk: 1) Sampling blind spots: we currently sample only by tenant_id and risk level, which can miss edge-case users with low volume but high privilege. 2) signed-batch key rotation: rotation events were not fully documented in earlier runs and some historic batches lack signer_key_id. 3) quarantine visibility: records routed to quarantine lacked the original request_id in the quarantine topic for a short window (resolved but need regression tests). 4) retention proofs: object-lock metadata was set inconsistently for a two-week window during migration to the new S3 bucket.
recommended_mitigations_and_acceptance_c: - Implement privilege-weighted sampling and run a 30-day backfill to detect missed high-privilege users. Acceptance: sampling tool produces >95% coverage for top-250 privileged principals. - Backfill signer metadata for historic batches where feasible and publish a rotation history table. Acceptance: no more than 0.1% of material batches lack signer metadata. - Add request_id to quarantine topic publisher and add unit test coverage. Acceptance: all quarantine records for a 7-day smoke run contain request_id. - Audit S3 retention metadata and remediate buckets with missing object-lock; produce a remediation ticket list. Acceptance: 100% of audit-critical buckets show compliant retention.
auditor_faq_prep: Q: How do you prove logs weren't modified after export? A: We publish signed batch manifests with SHA256 checksums and keep the signing private key in HSM; the auditor packet includes the public key and a repository of signatures. Q: Can you map a specific access decision to the end-user action? A: Yes — events contain request_id and session_id; for delegated actions we provide principal_chain entries. Q: What is your retention policy and how is it enforced? A: Retention is 7 years for audit-critical tenants, enforced via S3 object-lock + lifecycle; prove via object version metadata and lifecycle policy snapshots. Q: How do you handle key rotation? A: Rotation is recorded in rotation-log with effective_from timestamps and previous key fingerprints; manifests reference signer_key_id and rotation-log entries are included in the packet.
operational_checklist_for_pre-audit_run: - Run synthetic full-batch generator for each tenant in audit list. - Validate batch checksums and store verification logs. - Execute verify_batch.sh and publish results to SEC-412. - Export sample ES queries for ingestion_offset ranges. - Run regression tests for quarantine path. - Produce auditor packet and run internal peer review (security-compliance + infra). - File final packet in confluence and upload to secure Share with time-limited link.
